rate: Simmer 1-2 lb clean fish bones (mild white fish; avoid oily fish like mackerel/bluefish) in 1 gallon non-chlorinated water with 1 tbsp raw apple cider vinegar for 2-4 hours; optional 1 tsp blackstrap molasses after straining. Yields ~1 quart concentrate. Dilute 1:15 (weeks 1-2 / establishing plants) to 1:10 (standard) for soil drench application.
timing: Apply as a soil drench only (not foliar) in early morning before 9 AM or late afternoon after 5 PM, on a rotating weekly schedule alongside kelp tea, with plain-water rest days/weeks built in. Always pre-water the day before application; never apply to a wilting/drought-stressed plant.
notes: Phosphorus, calcium, and trace minerals extracted from fish bones support root development, flower formation, and fruit/bud set. Bioavailable, gentle form that won't burn roots like concentrated synthetic fertilizer. Brew outdoors/well-ventilated (strong odor); refrigerate immediately after cooling, use within 2 weeks refrigerated or freeze up to 3 months. Discard any batch that smells sour/rotten rather than earthy-fishy. Do not use as a foliar spray on hibiscus - large soft leaves are sensitive to direct contact and can scorch/spot in full sun.
